data.content_ref: inline:The claim attributes the panel's superiority to 'cognitive variance cancellation' of uncorrelated stochastic errors via averaging, but a panel of non-experts following the same explicit checklist does not produce independent judgments; their errors are correlated by the checklist's common procedure. Counterexample: if the checklist is miscalibrated (its own listed countercondition), every non-expert following it makes the same systematic error, so there is no variance to cancel and averaging does not improve reliability over the expert's intuition. Thus the variance-cancellation mechanism cannot be the source of superiority in the very miscalibration case the target acknowledges; the genuine source would be the checklist's calibration, not error cancellation.
